web.title: Ballon d'Or
web.description:
[Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi) has won the Ballon d'Or a record eight times, followed by [Cristiano Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo) with five. [Johan Cruyff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johan_Cruyff), [Michel Platini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michel_Platini) and [Marco van Basten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_van_Basten) have each won the award three times, while [Alfredo Di Stéfano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfredo_Di_St%C3%A9fano), [Franz Beckenbauer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franz_Beckenbauer), [Kevin Keegan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Keegan), [Karl-Heinz Rummenigge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Heinz_Rummenigge) and [Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronaldo_(Brazilian_footballer)) have each won it twice. [Ousmane Dembélé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ousmane_Demb%C3%A9l%C3%A9) is the current holder of the award, having won [its 69th edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Ballon_d'Or) in 2025.

## Overview
Liberia's [George Weah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Weah), the only African recipient, became the first non-European to win the award in [1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_Ballon_d'Or), the year that rules of eligibility were changed and the Ballon d'Or was expanded to include all players of any origin active at European clubs;[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballon_d%27Or#cite_note-BBCSport2008c-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballon_d%27Or#cite_note-NBCSports2023-13) [two years later](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_Ballon_d'Or), [Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronaldo_(Brazilian_footballer)) of Brazil became the first South American without a European citizenship to claim the award,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballon_d%27Or#cite_note-BBCSport2008c-12) and he is still the youngest winner ever at 21years, 96days old.

[Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi) holds the record for most Ballon d'Or wins with eight,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballon_d%27Or#cite_note-GuinnessWorldRecords2023-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballon_d%27Or#cite_note-Reuters2023-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballon_d%27Or#cite_note-LeParisien2023-20) while five-time winner [Cristiano Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo) earned the most nominations with eighteen. [[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballon_d%27Or#cite_note-Reuters2023-19) Three players have won the award three times each: [Johan Cruyff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johan_Cruyff), [Michel Platini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michel_Platini) and [Marco van Basten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_van_Basten). [[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballon_d%27Or#cite_note-UEFA2025-10)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballon_d%27Or#cite_note-IOC2025-21) With seven awards each, Dutch, German, and Portuguese players have won the second most Ballons d'Or, underneath Argentina and France in first with eight.

West German (1972) and Italian (1988– [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_Ballon_d'Or)) clubs achieved the same feat, including two individual years dominated by [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan) players (1988, [1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_Ballon_d'Or)), a unique record until Spanish clubs experienced an unprecedented dominance ( [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Ballon_d'Or)– [2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_FIFA_Ballon_d'Or), [2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_FIFA_Ballon_d'Or), 2016) and [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona) ( [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_FIFA_Ballon_d'Or)) became the second club to occupy the top-three.

## Winners
[![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/Lionel-Messi-Argentina-2022-FIFA-World-Cup_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Lionel-Messi-Argentina-2022-FIFA-World-Cup_%28cropped%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lionel-Messi-Argentina-2022-FIFA-World-Cup_(cropped).jpg) [Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi) has won a record eight Ballons d'Or across three different decades, and holds the record for most consecutive wins, with four between [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Ballon_d'Or) and [2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_FIFA_Ballon_d'Or).[![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8b/Cristiano_Ronaldo_WC2022_-_01_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Cristiano_Ronaldo_WC2022_-_01_%28cropped%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cristiano_Ronaldo_WC2022_-_01_(cropped).jpg) [Cristiano Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo) has been nominated for the Ballon d'Or a record eighteen times and is a five-time winner.[![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ed/Stanley_Matthews_1962_%28crop%29.jpg/250px-Stanley_Matthews_1962_%28crop%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Stanley_Matthews_1962_(crop).jpg) [Stanley Matthews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Matthews) was the inaugural recipient and remains the oldest winner of the award, aged 41years, 321days.[![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3b/Luis_Su%C3%A1rez_Miramontes.JPG/250px-Luis_Su%C3%A1rez_Miramontes.JPG)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Luis_Su%C3%A1rez_Miramontes.JPG) [Luis Suárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Su%C3%A1rez_(footballer,_born_1935)) was the first midfielder to win the award.[![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/LevYashin.JPG/250px-LevYashin.JPG)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:LevYashin.JPG) [Lev Yashin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lev_Yashin) is the only goalkeeper to have won the award.[![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cb/Johan_Cruijff_%281974%29.jpg/250px-Johan_Cruijff_%281974%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Johan_Cruijff_(1974).jpg) [Johan Cruyff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johan_Cruyff) was the first player to win the award three times.[![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/56/Franz_Beckenbauer_%281975%29.jpg/250px-Franz_Beckenbauer_%281975%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Franz_Beckenbauer_(1975).jpg) [Franz Beckenbauer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franz_Beckenbauer) is the only defender to have won the award twice.[![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/42/President_George_Weah_in_2019_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-President_George_Weah_in_2019_%28cropped%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_George_Weah_in_2019_(cropped).jpg) [George Weah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Weah)—the only African recipient—was the first non-European to win the award. [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f1/Ronaldo.jpeg/250px-Ronaldo.jpeg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ronaldo.jpeg) Two-time winner [Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronaldo_(Brazilian_footballer)) was the first South American to win the award and remains the youngest recipient, aged 21years, 96days.[![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/Ousmane_Dembele_France_v_Senegal_16_June_2026-341_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Ousmane_Dembele_France_v_Senegal_16_June_2026-341_%28cropped%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ousmane_Dembele_France_v_Senegal_16_June_2026-341_(cropped).jpg) [Ousmane Dembélé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ousmane_Demb%C3%A9l%C3%A9) is the current award holder.

# List of Ballon d’Or Winners
Britannica Editors

As of August 2025 [Lionel Messi](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Lionel-Messi) of [Argentina](https://www.britannica.com/place/Argentina) holds the record for the most awards, with eight, followed by [Portugal](https://www.britannica.com/place/Portugal)’s [Cristiano Ronaldo](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Cristiano-Ronaldo) with five. Three-time title winners include [Michel Platini](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Michel-Platini) of France and [Johan Cruyff](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Johan-Cruyff) and [Marco van Basten](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Marco-van-Basten), both from the [Netherlands](https://www.britannica.com/place/Netherlands).

U.S. and Reign FC (now Seattle Reign FC) player [Megan Rapinoe](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Megan-Rapinoe), and Spain and FC Barcelona Féminin players Alexia Putellas and [Aitana Bonmatí](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Aitana-Bonmati), are the other players who have won the award as of September 2025.
